topic: Work-Energy Theorem for a Variable Force
title: Changing Force? Work-Energy Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A trampoline pushes harder the deeper you sink. A rubber band pulls harder the more you stretch it. Diya squeezes a kitchen spring against a small block and lets go: the push starts strong and fades to nothing. F times d needs one steady force, so which force do we use to find the speed? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, plus JEE and NEET, we extend the work-energy theorem to a variable force.

On a live motion notebook a spring (k = 50 N/m, squeezed 0.4 m) launches a 2 kg block, with energy bars, a live readout and a force against position graph. A slow-mo replay cuts the push into four 10 cm strips: 1.75 + 1.25 + 0.75 + 0.25 = 4 J, exactly the block's kinetic energy at 2 m/s. We prove K_f - K_i = integral of F dx step by step from dK/dt = Fv, compare a steady push with a spring push side by side, and show link by link how area below the axis means negative work. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with F = 4x, the exam trap about using the biggest force, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.
